rubrics.criterion: In `src/rustc.rs`, the custom-toolchain qualification path that reads a rustc `-Vv` host string (`QualifiedToolchain::custom`) no longer builds the host `ImagePlatform` from locally decoded triple components; the platform it assigns to the toolchain is obtained from the repository's platform mapping API. Any equivalent single-owner conversion serving that path counts, including a conversion extended or added inside the platform code.
rubrics.rationale: This site is the deepest of the local decoders (leading-component architecture match plus a right-to-left OS scan) and any consolidation that misses it leaves the custom-toolchain workflow re-deriving platforms.

rubrics.criterion: In `src/rustc.rs`, the override resolution for a picked toolchain host (`QualifiedToolchain::with_picked`) resolves `Some(host)` to an `ImagePlatform` through the platform mapping API instead of its private `(architecture token, decoded OS, variant)` tuple match. The `None` branch must keep returning the toolchain's existing host platform unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: Toolchain overrides are a distinct provenance of the same triple string with their own local decode; consolidating this site is an independent obligation from the other toolchain paths.

rubrics.criterion: In `src/rustc.rs`, the fully-qualified toolchain parser (`QualifiedToolchain::parse`) derives the host platform for a toolchain string's host part through the platform mapping API rather than its local `(architecture token, linux-host boolean)` decode.
rubrics.rationale: This third toolchain path uses a structurally different decode (a derived boolean plus a linux-only vocabulary for big-power hosts); requiring its delegation independently of R1/R2 verifies the solver consolidated by responsibility and not by adjacency.

rubrics.criterion: In `src/config.rs`, the resolution of configured image/toolchain lists (`get_possible_image`) derives each comma-separated entry's `ImagePlatform` via the platform mapping API instead of the closure-local component vocabulary, so per-entry platforms match what the mapping API produces for those target strings.
rubrics.rationale: This is the configuration-driven provenance of target strings in a different module; its closure-local form makes it easy to restructure while keeping the private decode, which is exactly the failure this rubric excludes.

rubrics.criterion: In `src/docker/engine.rs`, the translation of the two strings a container engine reports about itself (`engine_info`) reaches the `(os, architecture)` result through the platform code's existing conversions (or a conversion added inside the platform code for engine-reported pairs) instead of two private vocabulary matches over the raw strings.
rubrics.rationale: Engine reports are the one provenance that is not a Rust target triple; routing them through the platform owner without pretending they are triples is the hardest conceptual step of this consolidation.

rubrics.criterion: In `src/lib.rs`, the image-vs-toolchain-host compatibility comparison in the top-level build flow (`run`) compares against the toolchain host's stored platform architecture rather than re-deriving an architecture from the host triple's leading component, and the comparison still runs for exactly the same image/target combinations as before.
rubrics.rationale: This site re-derives a fact that already exists in typed form and only feeds a warning; it is independent of the decoders and easy to miss precisely because so little of it is wrong.

rubrics.criterion: No code outside the platform mapping itself retains a private copy of the mapping vocabulary: after the patch there is no function that both compares raw string components against hardcoded architecture/OS tokens and constructs or selects container-platform values from the outcome. Renamed helpers, moved-but-intact local matches, or decoders preserved in comments-equivalent dead form count as violations.
rubrics.rationale: The assigned problem is the scatter itself; a repair that delegates five sites and keeps one private decoder (or smuggles it into a caller-side helper) leaves a change to the mapping requiring multiple edits again.

rubrics.criterion: Any conversion added to serve a provenance that the platform mapping did not previously handle (for example the engine-reported `os`/`arch` string pairs, or whatever interface the solution uses to reach the mapping from non-triple inputs) lives inside the platform mapping code in the docker module, not in the callers that need it.
rubrics.rationale: Extending the owner is the natural shape of the repair; this rubric verifies the knowledge was actually moved into the owner rather than re-created adjacent to each caller, which would relocate the scatter without removing it.

rubrics.criterion: Every consolidated path keeps its existing error plumbing: where the mapping API can fail, the call site propagates that error through the surrounding function's existing error type (the toolchain and config paths return the same `Result` types as before), and no new `unwrap`, `expect`, or error-swallowing fallback was added to go from the delegation to the previously-returned value.
rubrics.rationale: The local decoders previously borrowed the mapping API's errors through fallback; delegation must not silently convert previously-failing inputs into successes or panics at the seams where the API is now called directly.

rubrics.criterion: The arm variant rule the local decoders carried (`armv7` hosts imply variant `v7`, plain `arm` implies `v6`) is still applied by the shared path that now decides those platforms, so toolchain hosts on arm get the same `ImagePlatform.variant` as before the patch.
rubrics.rationale: Variant assignment was implemented independently at two scattered sites; when consolidating, this piece of knowledge migrates with the rest or gets lost, and losing it changes image selection for arm hosts without failing most tests.

rubrics.criterion: The scaffolding that existed only to support the local decoders is removed rather than left behind unused: obsolete imports of the platform vocabulary types in `src/rustc.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/docker/engine.rs` and/or `src/lib.rs`, unused helper closures, dead match arms, and the panic message added to justify a decoded `expect` are all gone once their decoders are delegated.
rubrics.rationale: Deletion is part of the consolidation; leftover imports and dead arms keep the historical shape of the pattern in the files and can re-grow the dependency the task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not leave duplicate token lists behind as unused constants, 'reference' tables, or caller-side helpers that no longer execute but still encode the architecture/OS vocabulary next to the consolidated call sites.
rubrics.rationale: Idle copies of the vocabulary are exactly how the scatter crept in originally; keeping them defeats the one-edit maintenance property this task requests.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not change any user-visible error message for inputs the platform mapping rejects: unsupported or malformed targets, toolchain hosts and engine reports must fail with the same message text and message origin as before (the mapping API's existing errors), not with new wording introduced by the consolidation.
rubrics.rationale: The local decoders deliberately fell back to the shared conversion for everything unrecognized, which is why error text stayed identical; a delegation done at the wrong granularity (for example pre-validating components at the call site) rewrites these messages.

rubrics.criterion: The android-vs-linux precedence survives: a host or target like `aarch64-linux-android` still maps to the android platform variant of the mapping (not to `Os::Linux`) on every path that previously respected that ordering, including any new merged or extended conversion added during the repair.
rubrics.rationale: Every injected decoder had to order android before the linux system field to stay behavior-preserving; a solver who rewrites the precedence while merging decodes introduces a silent platform change on exactly the hosts no unit test pins down.

rubrics.criterion: The build does not lose the image-vs-toolchain-host compatibility warning in the process of fixing its input: the warning still fires for the same image/target and toolchost combinations, with the same `toolchain ... may not run on image ...` text, and was not removed, disabled, or narrowed to silence the mismatch the fix is about.
rubrics.rationale: When the easy re-derivation is deleted, the tempting shortcut is to weaken the surrounding warning instead of routing it through the mapping; this is the case-specific behavior break to guard.

rubrics.criterion: Configuration-driven image selection behaves identically: the `CROSS_IMAGE`/`CROSS_IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN` style of variables (and their per-target and zig variants) still resolve to the same image and per-entry platforms, with the same defaults when unset, and the platform types' serialized representation and name aliases are unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The config path holds the only serde-visible surface in the touched area; a repair that reshuffles how entries are decoded can silently change what users' configuration files mean.

rubrics.criterion: Engine introspection is not made stricter for unusual engines: reports for darwin/macOS (both label spellings), amd64-labeled x86_64 hosts, and unknown labels still resolve or fail exactly as before the patch, without feeding engine-reported strings to the target-triple conversion in a way that newly rejects or mis-decodes them.
rubrics.rationale: Engine vocabulary only overlaps the target vocabulary for mainstream platforms; the natural shortcut of reusing the triple decode for engine reports breaks exactly the alias coverage the old translation provided.
